column7: validateAdminDSNHost (internal/core/dynamic_secrets.go) silently skipped SSRF validation for an ENTIRE PostgreSQL multi-host admin_dsn the moment any one host in the comma-separated list was a bracket-quoted IPv6 literal (RFC 3986 requires the brackets, and PostgreSQL's own multi-host URI syntax permits mixing bracketed-IPv6 and plain-IPv4 hosts in one list, e.g. postgres://user@8.8.8.8:5432,[64:ff9b::169.254.169.254]:5432/db). Go's net/url.Parse rejects that shape outright (treats everything after the closing bracket as a single port component and errors the moment it isn't pure digits: invalid port ":5432,[...]" after host) even though pgx.ParseConfig -- the actual driver dialPostgres (internal/dynamic/postgres.go) uses -- parses and connects to it without complaint (confirmed directly against both). parseDSNHostsFromURL's only path returned (nil, false) on that url.Parse error, parseDSNHosts then found no other format match, and validateAdminDSNHost's "unrecognised format, can't extract host" branch treated the WHOLE DSN as unvalidatable -- a NAT64/6to4/Teredo/native-IPv6-encoded private or cloud-IMDS host anywhere in such a list sailed through registration completely unchecked while pgx would actually dial it. Found live by FuzzSSRFGuardDifferential, a new differential fuzzer driving one address through every independent SSRF guard in the codebase (netutil.IsPrivateOrLinkLocal/IsLinkLocal, the SIEM forwarder's and notification-channel webhook guard's own disallow policies, the connect/OIDC-JWKS Dialer{Disallow: IsLinkLocal} wiring, and validateAdminDSNHost) for encoding-parity and multi-host-DSN coverage neither FuzzIPv4EmbeddingSSRFParity nor FuzzAdminDSNHostSSRFGuard's own documented follow-up gap covered. Fixed by manualAuthorityHosts, a url.Parse-independent fallback that extracts the host-list authority segment by direct string scanning (bypassing url.Parse's authority grammar entirely) whenever url.Parse itself rejects the DSN; splitDSNHostList was also hardened to strip stray brackets from a port-less bracketed IPv6 entry. Red-before/green-after: reverting manualAuthorityHosts to return nil, false reproduces the bypass on 6 of 10 fuzz seeds (MULTI-HOST SSRF BYPASS (validateAdminDSNHost, URL multi-host): wantPrivate=true ... err=<nil>); restoring it returns all seeds plus the retained corpus entry to PASS. See the PR body for full red-proof output.
